The test image shows **soybean stems** with dense, small black specks covering the surface, giving a charcoal-sprinkled appearance. The stems look dry and mature.

From the part index, stem candidates are: Anthracnose, Brown_Stem_Rot, Charcoal_Rot, Diaporthe, Fusarium, Green_stem_disorder, Phytophthora, Pythium_damping_off, Rhizoctonia, Tobacco_Streak_Virus, White_Mold.

Top candidates based on symptoms: **Charcoal_Rot** (microsclerotia giving charcoal-sprinkled look), **Anthracnose** (black acervuli on stems), **Diaporthe** (black pycnidia in linear rows).

Let me view references one at a time, starting with one from each top candidate.
Charcoal_Rot reference shows gray streaks and peeling epidermis but not the same dense black speckling pattern. Let me check Anthracnose stem.

Anthracnose stems show dark irregular lesions with some black speckling, but the pattern differs from the very dense, uniform speckling in the test image. Let me check Diaporthe (though it's not in the 25 classes... wait, let me check).

Diaporthe is not in the 25 possible classes. Let me check Charcoal_Rot stem reference #2, then branch to other candidates.

This Charcoal_Rot reference is very similar - gray stems with scattered black microsclerotia giving the charcoal-sprinkled appearance. Strong match. Let me continue checking other candidates for completeness.
Anthracnose here shows dark patches on green stems with pods - very different from the test image. Let me check White_Mold, Fusarium, Rhizoctonia, and Tobacco_Streak_Virus stems.
White_Mold shows fluffy white mold and dark sclerotia on green stems - not matching. Let me check more candidates.
Rhizoctonia shows reddish-brown cankers at soil line on young stems - not matching.
Tobacco_Streak_Virus shows discoloration at nodes on green stems - not matching.

Phytophthora shows chocolate-brown stem discoloration from soil line up - not matching the dense black speckling pattern.

All 8 reference views used. The test image most closely matches **Charcoal_Rot reference #2** (Soybean_Dise_49.jpg), which showed the same characteristic pattern: gray stems densely covered with small black specks (microsclerotia) giving a charcoal-sprinkled appearance. This is the hallmark diagnostic feature of Charcoal Rot in soybean.

Key evidence:
- Dense small black specks (microsclerotia) covering the stem surface
- Gray/bleached stem appearance underneath
- Dry, mature stem tissue
- No fluffy mold (rules out White_Mold), no linear rows of pycnidia, no lesions at soil line
